$comment: The two function-privilege classes this repository will not let drift.

internalOnly: SECURITY DEFINER, callable as an RPC, and executable by NONE of anon, authenticated or service_role. Only the database itself may call these. A function that loses its revokes DROPS OUT of this list, which is the regression we are guarding: adding a parameter means DROP and CREATE, and a created function starts with proacl NULL, which in Postgres means EXECUTE TO PUBLIC. enqueue_kit_operation lost its revokes exactly that way on 2026-10-10.

publicExecutable: SECURITY DEFINER, callable, and proacl IS NULL. Anyone may call these and they run as their owner. Deliberately not asserted empty: is_admin() is read by RLS policies and must be callable by whoever the policy is evaluated for, and it only ever reports on the caller.

serviceRoleOnly: SECURITY DEFINER, callable, and executable by service_role and nobody else — the internals an Edge Function may reach and a browser may not. get_user_id_by_email dropped out of this set in production because nothing ever granted service_role (ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES decides what a new function starts with, and that depends on which role created it), so the users Edge Function recovery branch answered 500. 20261010210000 states the posture in the chain.
Browser-callable RPCs appear in neither list: they hold explicit grants, so they are not internal-only and not NULL-ACL.
